arrival.note: He is in the settlement by 1831, when he stands surety on the ferry bond. Nothing dates his coming.

lives_at.note: Andreas's residents list places 'James Kinzie and family' near Wentworth's tavern and this dataset's james_kinzie_house sits in that row, south of the tavern, on the strength of the same clause. Inferred rather than documented because the building record itself calls its evidence 'a single clause' and grades its own position inferred.

works_at.note: NOT ATTESTED AT THE SCENE DATE. He built the Green Tree and Chester Ingersoll kept it; he built a tavern on the west side of the South Branch and a Mr Crook kept it. This dataset holds james_kinzie_house as his residence and that is a lives_at, not a works_at.

present_on_scene_date.note: Continuous in the Chicago record across the period.

persons.name: James Kinzie

occupation.note: 'James Kinzie and family ... resided near Wentworth's tavern' in the list Andreas prints of the settlement's residents; he is a candidate at the 1833 town election and takes five votes. He built the Green Tree Tavern in 1833 and leased it, and he was surety on Mark Beaubien's ferry bond of 6 June 1831.

persons.note: A BUILDER OF TAVERNS RATHER THAN A KEEPER OF THEM, which is why his structure links are thin. Andreas has him building the Green Tree and leasing it to David Clock; Charles Butler in August 1833 lodged at a tavern on the west side of the South Branch 'erected by James Kinzie, but kept by a Mr. Crook (?)' - the question mark is Andreas's or Butler's, not this project's. He is a half-brother to John H. and Robert A. Kinzie.

resident_research.evidence_for: Early Chicago civic/business histories distinguish James Kinzie from the other Kinzie men and connect him with Wolf Point, auctioneering and early town affairs. The pass keeps those identities separate rather than treating the surname as a household merge rule.
resident_research.notes: Early Chicago civic/business histories distinguish James Kinzie from the other Kinzie men and connect him with Wolf Point, auctioneering and early town affairs. The pass keeps those identities separate rather than treating the surname as a household merge rule.

research_note: A HOUSEHOLD WITH A FAMILY IN THE SOURCE AND NO PEOPLE IN THE RECORD. Andreas's list says 'James Kinzie and family' and this parcel writes one person, because naming a wife or counting children on the strength of the word 'family' is the exact move the grade vocabulary forbids. THE HONEST READING OF THIS RECORD is that it stands for at least three or four people and can defend only one.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry.
